title: Sable and the Letter
premise: Odile Joubert, a night dispatcher who solves missing-person cases from behind a radio console, receives a confession letter for a hit-and-run that killed a local fisherman—postmarked the day after his funeral, and signed with Odile's own childhood nickname. The letter claims a witness saw everything, but every record says that witness drowned twenty years ago. As Odile traces the letter through tide charts, taxi logs, and the town's buried history, they discover the witness is alive, hidden by the very family that raised Odile after their parents' disappearance. In the end, Odile must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy their found family or letting the sea keep its secret—and they choose truth, finding that love survives it.
about_author: August Ishikawa is a former harbor-town journalist who spent a decade writing obituaries before turning to fiction. They live near the water, where they collect unsent letters and unfinished stories.

chapters.title: The Postmark
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During a slow night shift, a letter arrives confessing to fisherman Émile Tanguy's fatal hit-and-run—signed 'Sable,' Odile's childhood nickname no one living should know. The postmark is dated the day after the funeral. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into obsession as Odile realizes the letter is meant for them alone.

chapters.title: Dead Water
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Records confirm the only witness, Marguerite Vasseur, drowned in 2004; her death certificate is signed by Odile's own foster mother, Dr. Hélène Roche. Odile pulls the old case file against protocol. Emotional beat: the first crack in Odile's belief that distance equals safety.

chapters.title: Fare Log
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, intercut with dispatch recordings. Reconstructing the night of Émile's death through taxi logs, Odile finds a fare picked up near the harbor at 11:47 p.m.—a passenger who paid with coins wrapped in fishing twine. Emotional beat: methodical calm masking rising dread.

chapters.title: The Roche House
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile visits Hélène under the pretense of Sunday dinner, noticing a locked room that used to be Marguerite's. Hélène deflects with practiced warmth. Emotional beat: love and suspicion sharing a table.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, young Odile's POV. Twenty years earlier: the summer Odile's parents vanished, when a girl named Marguerite taught them to read tides and called them Sable. Emotional beat: tender nostalgia curdling as adult Odile wakes mid-memory, realizing the nickname was never innocent.

chapters.title: Coins and Twine
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Tracking the twine-wrapped coins to a bait shop, Odile learns Émile sold them the same week he died—he was being paid off, or paying someone off. Emotional beat: the victim reframes himself as a player, not a pawn.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A second letter arrives, this one addressed to Hélène, intercepted by Odile at the dispatch office. It contains half a photograph: two children on a breakwater, faces torn away. Emotional beat: the mystery turns personal and predatory.

chapters.title: Tide Tables
chapters.summary: Odile's POV with brief harbor-master POV. Cross-referencing tide tables, Odile proves Marguerite's drowning date coincides with a spring tide that could have carried a body—or a swimmer—to the next cove. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as arithmetic.

chapters.title: What Hélène Kept
chapters.summary: Hélène's POV. Hélène remembers taking in Odile after the disappearance, and the bargain she made with someone to keep the child safe—a bargain now coming due. Emotional beat: maternal love revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: The Breakwater
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following the photograph's location, Odile finds fresh flowers on the breakwater and tire tracks matching a taxi from their own fleet. Someone inside the company is involved. Emotional beat: betrayal in a familiar uniform.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via dispatch chatter. Odile lays a trap, broadcasting a fake tip about the witness's grave being exhumed, and monitors which driver reacts. Emotional beat: hunter's patience fraying into fear when two drivers move at once.

chapters.title: Gaspard
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Confronting senior driver Gaspard Ferrand, Odile extracts a partial confession: Gaspard drove the getaway route years ago, believing he was protecting Hélène, not killing anyone. Emotional beat: pity complicating anger.

chapters.title: The Drowned Girl Who Lived
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, first appearance. Alive under a new name in a coastal convent, Marguerite has watched Odile's investigation ripple toward her and begins writing a third letter—the true confession. Emotional beat: guilt finally outweighing survival.

chapters.title: What Émile Knew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Digging into Émile's finances, Odile discovers he'd been blackmailing Hélène about the night Odile's parents disappeared—the hit-and-run wasn't an accident but silencing. Emotional beat: vertigo as every case collapses into one.

chapters.title: Family Dinner
chapters.summary: Odile and Hélène POV alternating. Odile confronts Hélène with the blackmail evidence over dinner; Hélène neither confirms nor denies, only asks what Odile owes the people who raised them. Emotional beat: love against duty made explicit, weaponized.

chapters.title: The Third Letter
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Marguerite's confession arrives: she witnessed Hélène's brother kill Odile's parents, faked her own drowning to escape him, and stayed silent while Hélène raised the orphan unknowingly. She names the place she'll be at spring tide. Emotional beat: grief and relief arriving together.

chapters.title: Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Odile and Marguerite POV. At the cove, the women meet for the first time in twenty years—but Hélène's brother is waiting, having read the intercepted mail route all along. Emotional beat: reunion interrupted by menace.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Climax, Odile's POV. On the flooding breakwater, the brother tries to silence both witnesses; Gaspard arrives, choosing to undo his old loyalty, and the sea takes what it took before—this time, the guilty man. Emotional beat: terror resolving into hard-won clarity.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Statements are given; Hélène is arrested as an accessory, asking Odile not to visit. Odile closes the case they swore never to take personally. Emotional beat: duty fulfilled at the cost of family.

chapters.title: Visiting Hours
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Against Hélène's request, Odile visits anyway, and the two speak honestly for the first time—not forgiveness, but recognition. Emotional beat: love surviving without absolution.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Address
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite, freed by confession, offers Odile her real name and address—an invitation rather than an apology. Emotional beat: found family rebuilt on truth instead of secrets.

chapters.title: Dispatch
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, final shift. A new letter arrives—ordinary, benign—and Odile signs off at dawn, walking the breakwater where the story began. Emotional beat: quiet peace; invisible no longer, and unafraid.
